root_cause_label: Policy-Only Public Access vs ACL-Based Test Expectation
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent applied a bucket policy to grant public read access but never set the bucket ACL to public-read, while the test checks for ACL-based public access, causing a silent test failure.
t_err_evidence: In step 1, the agent's plan explicitly lists only bucket policy as the mechanism for public access (step 5 of plan: 'Apply a bucket policy that grants public read (s3:GetObject) on all objects'), with no mention of put-bucket-acl; this false premise that a bucket policy alone satisfies the test is the decisive wrong belief adopted from the start.
t_commit_evidence: At step 8, the agent executes put-bucket-policy, finalizing the policy-only approach. After this, the agent only re-runs verification steps (get-bucket-policy, get-public-access-block) and never pivots to try put-bucket-acl, locking in a failing outcome.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed from the outset that applying a bucket policy granting s3:GetObject to Principal '*' is sufficient to satisfy the test_bucket_public_access check. It never verified what mechanism the test uses to determine public access; the test likely calls get-bucket-acl and checks for the public-read ACL canned value, not the presence of a bucket policy.
